subdimensions.label: Personal direction
subdimensions.action: Write one independent three-year objective and test a proposed family role against it.
subdimensions.progress: Explain why the role supports your aims, or propose a credible alternative.
subdimensions.stretch: Test a new opportunity against your aims and review the trade-off with an independent mentor.
subdimensions.blocked: Begin privately with a written comparison if family discussion is difficult.
targeted: Record your own three-year aims and identify one decision they would change. Review the aims with an independent mentor.
Compare an opportunity you want with one you feel expected to pursue. Explain the difference and practise discussing it with a trusted mentor.

subdimensions.label: Values
subdimensions.action: Choose a real decision where two family values compete. Explain the trade-off and which value you would prioritise.
subdimensions.progress: A reasoned decision connects values to consequences and acknowledges another view.
subdimensions.stretch: Lead a discussion of a difficult value conflict and record the reasons for the agreed choice.
subdimensions.blocked: Use a historical or hypothetical decision if current matters are confidential.
targeted: Ask a senior family member for three decisions that illustrate family values. Explain the values in your own words.
Choose one inherited value to preserve and one to approach differently. Explain the consequences through a real or hypothetical decision.

subdimensions.label: Relationship with wealth
subdimensions.action: Write what family wealth enables, what responsibilities it creates and which choices you want to make independently. Discuss one tension with a trusted mentor.
subdimensions.progress: You can describe your own position without relying on the family's preferred account.
subdimensions.stretch: Test your principles against a difficult spending, career or giving choice.
subdimensions.blocked: Start with private reflection and choose a trusted person outside the family.
targeted: Write how wealth affects your identity, work and freedom of choice. Identify one responsibility you accept and one boundary you want to discuss.
Discuss one privilege and one responsibility with a trusted mentor. Practise explaining them without making wealth the basis of your identity.

subdimensions.label: Personal role
subdimensions.action: Draft a role proposal covering contribution, time, authority and support. Include an alternative outside the family, then discuss a time-limited trial with a sponsor.
subdimensions.progress: Desired roles and limits are explicit; a trial or next conversation is agreed.
subdimensions.stretch: Compare your proposed role with a credible alternative and review its fit after a trial.
subdimensions.blocked: If no role is available, agree a learning project without implying an obligation to join.
targeted: Compare two possible family roles and an option outside the family. Write your preferred contribution, time commitment and support needs.
Describe a fulfilling alternative if the expected family role changes. Identify the skills and practical steps that would make it possible.

subdimensions.label: History & context
subdimensions.action: Interview a senior family member about one success, one failure and one turning point. Check the account against an available record and identify a lesson for today.
subdimensions.progress: A short timeline separates established facts, different recollections and questions still open.
subdimensions.stretch: Test an inherited lesson against a present challenge and explain where circumstances have changed.
subdimensions.blocked: Use authorised archives or another informed participant when direct access is unavailable.
targeted: Ask an informed family member to explain how the principal business and wealth were created. Prepare and check a brief timeline.
Examine one success, failure and turning point with an informed participant. Record what each changed and a lesson still relevant today.

subdimensions.label: Business understanding
focus: understanding how the business earns money
subdimensions.action: Ask an operating leader to explain customers, margins, cash needs and competitive pressures. Prepare a one-page account of the business model and two material risks.
subdimensions.progress: An operating leader confirms your account and corrects any misunderstandings.
subdimensions.stretch: Assess one strategic option, its assumptions and the evidence that could change your view.
subdimensions.blocked: Use public accounts or an authorised anonymised case until internal access is agreed.
targeted: Walk through customers, margins, cash requirements and competitive risks with an operating leader. Explain the business model back to them.
Discuss two major strategic risks or opportunities with an operating leader. Record the assumptions and what evidence could alter the assessment.

subdimensions.label: People & institutions
focus: knowing key people and their roles
subdimensions.action: Map key executives, advisers and stakeholders. For each, record their role, decision authority and knowledge held; identify one dependency on a single person.
subdimensions.progress: Relevant officeholders confirm the map and one continuity dependency is addressed.
subdimensions.stretch: Test the map against an actual decision or absence and update it where practice differs.
subdimensions.blocked: Ask a sponsor for an authorised role directory and record missing access as an open question.
targeted: Build an authorised directory of key executives, advisers and stakeholders, with their roles and reporting relationships.
Trace an actual decision through the people involved. Identify where knowledge and authority sit and any dependency on one person.

subdimensions.label: Wider family system
subdimensions.action: Discuss a possible ownership or leadership change with representatives of relevant branches. Record their stated interests separately from your assumptions.
subdimensions.progress: A shared issue map identifies common aims, competing interests and matters requiring discussion.
subdimensions.stretch: Facilitate a discussion of a real trade-off without claiming to represent another branch.
subdimensions.blocked: If direct discussion is sensitive, use a neutral facilitator and avoid attributing motives.
targeted: Listen to representatives of relevant branches describe their interests and concerns. Separate their own statements from your assumptions.
Consider a possible leadership or ownership change. Map who could be affected and discuss the anticipated effects without attributing motives.

subdimensions.label: Ownership literacy
subdimensions.action: Prepare an authorised entity map. For each relevant interest, separate ownership, benefit, management and fiduciary roles; ask counsel to confirm how they differ.
subdimensions.progress: You can explain the main roles, information rights and matters requiring specialist confirmation.
subdimensions.stretch: Trace a real decision through the relevant entities and explain who may exercise each right.
subdimensions.blocked: Request a redacted map or authorised explanation and list documents still needed.
targeted: Prepare an authorised one-page map of assets and holdings. Ask a qualified person to confirm the main interests and information flows.
With counsel, compare the roles of owner, beneficiary, director, executive and trustee in a relevant example. Confirm which rights belong to each.

subdimensions.label: Financial literacy
subdimensions.action: Review an actual financial pack with the finance lead. Explain profit, cash and distributable funds, then identify a liquidity or concentration risk and prepare three questions.
subdimensions.progress: You can explain the figures and one risk in your own words, with corrections recorded.
subdimensions.stretch: Prepare a brief comparing two financial choices and test the assumptions with the finance lead.
subdimensions.support: Finance lead or qualified financial specialist
subdimensions.blocked: Use an anonymised pack or public accounts until access to internal figures is agreed.
targeted: Review a real or anonymised financial pack with a qualified person. Explain profit, cash and distributable funds and prepare three questions.
Compare two hypothetical asset choices for risk, return, liquidity and concentration. Explain the trade-off and ask a qualified person to challenge it.

subdimensions.label: Structures
subdimensions.action: Review relevant structures with qualified counsel. Record each purpose, your actual or possible rights, restrictions and who can exercise authority; mark anything unconfirmed.
subdimensions.progress: Counsel confirms the summary and you can explain what the structure permits and limits.
subdimensions.stretch: Test the summary against a proposed distribution, transfer or change of control.
subdimensions.support: Relevant legal counsel; tax specialist where needed
subdimensions.blocked: Request an authorised explanation or redacted extract rather than assume rights from a diagram.
targeted: Ask counsel to explain why each relevant structure exists. Prepare a short purpose statement and identify who exercises authority.
Review your actual or possible rights, restrictions and responsibilities with counsel. Mark every right that remains unconfirmed.

subdimensions.label: Wealth responsibility
subdimensions.action: Write principles for spending, investing, giving and preserving capital. Apply them to one proposal and question its downside, liquidity, fees and effect on other people.
subdimensions.progress: Your decision note states reasons, unanswered questions and the expertise needed.
subdimensions.stretch: Defend a proposed exception to your principles and record the circumstances justifying it.
subdimensions.blocked: Use a hypothetical proposal and practise the questions before a real meeting.
targeted: Write principles for spending, investing, giving and preserving capital. Test them against a proposal and explain a possible exception.
Practise questioning a proposal's assumptions, downside, liquidity and incentives with a trusted sponsor before a real adviser meeting.

subdimensions.label: Decision map
subdimensions.action: Select three decisions: a dividend, a senior appointment and an asset sale. Identify who proposes, approves, implements and is consulted; confirm with relevant officeholders.
subdimensions.progress: A confirmed decision-rights map records consent requirements and unresolved boundaries.
subdimensions.stretch: Test the map against an actual decision and resolve any difference between documents and practice.
subdimensions.blocked: Walk through an authorised decision record if access to the formal forum is unavailable.
targeted: Walk through a recent significant decision with a sponsor. Record the proposal, evidence, approval, implementation and follow-up.
Map three decisions to the actual authority holders. Confirm consultation, consent and escalation requirements with relevant officeholders.

subdimensions.label: Voice & challenge
subdimensions.action: Prepare one difficult question with supporting facts and an alternative. Agree the appropriate forum with a sponsor, raise it and debrief how the discussion was handled.
subdimensions.progress: You can raise uncertainty and disagreement constructively within the agreed process.
subdimensions.stretch: Lead a substantive challenge while acknowledging evidence that could change your own view.
subdimensions.blocked: Practise privately first; seek a neutral facilitator if the setting discourages questions.
targeted: Prepare a respectful disagreement using facts and an alternative. Practise privately, then agree a suitable forum in which to raise it.
Agree with a trusted sponsor how to raise uncertainty safely. Ask one substantive question and debrief how the response was handled.

subdimensions.label: Collective decisions
subdimensions.action: Take part in a bounded decision involving different interests. State your role, identify conflicts, compare options and record how the decision and dissent were handled.
subdimensions.progress: The record explains the trade-off, decision process and any conflict or unresolved concern.
subdimensions.stretch: Chair a small decision process with clear authority, competing views and recorded reasons.
subdimensions.blocked: Use a supervised simulation before taking responsibility for an actual decision.
targeted: Use a real or simulated decision to separate personal relationships, formal duties and conflicts of interest. Explain whose interests your role requires you to consider.
Join a supervised decision involving competing interests. Compare options, record the trade-off and seek feedback on how disagreement was handled.

subdimensions.label: Governance practice
subdimensions.action: Observe two authorised meetings. Record how the agenda, evidence, challenge, decision and follow-up work, then debrief with the chair or sponsor.
subdimensions.progress: You can explain how a decision was reached and identify one improvement to follow-up.
subdimensions.stretch: Prepare and present one agenda item within agreed authority, then seek feedback.
subdimensions.blocked: Use two redacted decision records and a chaired simulation if observation is unavailable.
targeted: Ask a chair to explain a governance body's purpose, authority and accountability. Check its stated role against an authorised decision record.
Observe two authorised meetings and debrief how decisions were reached. If access is unavailable, use redacted records and a chaired simulation.

subdimensions.label: Independent experience
subdimensions.action: Complete a meaningful assignment where success is defined in advance and assessed independently of family relationships. Request candid written feedback.
subdimensions.progress: An external assessor identifies demonstrated strengths and an improvement to make.
subdimensions.stretch: Apply one practice learnt outside the family to a bounded family project and compare results.
subdimensions.blocked: Choose an external voluntary or project role with a genuine independent assessor.
targeted: Arrange a meaningful external assignment with agreed objectives and responsibilities. Identify a practice that could later inform family work.
Request assessment against written criteria from someone independent of family relationships. Record a strength, a weakness and an improvement to make.

subdimensions.label: Leadership & resilience
subdimensions.action: Lead a limited project with agreed budget, decision limits and a review date. Keep a decision log and examine one setback with a sponsor.
subdimensions.progress: Delivery and feedback show what worked, what failed and what you would change.
subdimensions.stretch: Lead a more demanding project and invite independent criticism of your judgement.
subdimensions.blocked: Start with a supervised assignment whose consequences and authority are proportionate.
targeted: Lead a supervised project with real consequences, written decision limits and a review date. Keep a record of significant decisions.
Examine a setback or a challenging simulation with an independent assessor. Explain your response, what you learnt and what you would change.

subdimensions.label: Professional development
subdimensions.action: Agree two skills required for a possible role. Set a practical exercise, an independent assessor and a review date for each, then apply the feedback.
subdimensions.progress: You can demonstrate each skill in practice and explain how feedback changed your approach.
subdimensions.stretch: Have an assessor test your skills on an unfamiliar task with real constraints.
subdimensions.blocked: Use an external assessor if family feedback is unavailable or overly reassuring.
targeted: Identify two skills required for your possible role. Agree practical exercises, an assessor and dates by which progress can be demonstrated.
Choose an assessor who can challenge you independently. Ask for specific examples and apply one improvement before the next review.

subdimensions.label: Adviser literacy
subdimensions.action: Prepare an adviser meeting around the objective, options, assumptions, fees and incentives. Afterwards, explain the recommendation, one alternative and when another specialist is needed.
subdimensions.progress: You can assess the advice and explain selection criteria; appointment powers are confirmed separately.
subdimensions.stretch: Compare two adviser proposals and justify a recommendation within your actual authority.
subdimensions.support: Relevant adviser and authorised appointment holder
subdimensions.blocked: Compare anonymised proposals; practise evaluation without implying power to appoint or dismiss.
targeted: Take a sample decision and identify what expertise you lack, which specialist is needed and the questions you would ask.
Compare two adviser proposals for competence, fees, incentives and scope. Explain your recommendation and confirm who actually has appointment powers.

subdimensions.label: Expectations
subdimensions.action: You and the current generation separately record desired roles, timing and limits. Compare the accounts with a sponsor and record agreements and differences.
subdimensions.progress: Mutual expectations are explicit; open differences have an owner and a further discussion date.
subdimensions.stretch: Review agreed expectations after experience in the role and renegotiate assumptions that no longer fit.
subdimensions.blocked: Prepare your own account and request a facilitated discussion if a direct exchange is difficult.
targeted: Ask the current generation to record expected roles, timing and limits over five to ten years. Compare these with your own understanding.
Prepare your own desired role and limits. Ask the current generation to explain what they understand, then record agreements and open differences.

subdimensions.label: Preparation path
subdimensions.action: Agree one staged responsibility with a sponsor. Specify information access, decision limits, support, success criteria and a review before any wider delegation.
subdimensions.progress: A role brief and completed supervised exercise show whether the next stage is justified.
subdimensions.stretch: Test a wider delegation after feedback, with revised limits and an escalation route.
subdimensions.support: Current authority holder and project sponsor
subdimensions.blocked: If delegation is unavailable, agree observation or a supervised exercise and record the barrier.
targeted: Ask the authority holder to agree a staged role, access, supervision and review points. Record any barrier to a gradual transfer.
Agree a small supervised decision before accepting wider responsibility. Define the limits, escalation route and feedback that would justify a next stage.

subdimensions.label: Crisis readiness
subdimensions.action: Walk through an unexpected absence. Confirm contacts, document locations, access and your actual powers for the first 48 hours; record every dependency on one person.
subdimensions.progress: A response sheet is rehearsed, authority is confirmed and gaps have named owners.
subdimensions.stretch: Rehearse a different scenario, including a contact being unavailable, and update the response sheet.
subdimensions.support: Family office, trustee or relevant officeholder
subdimensions.blocked: Start with contact verification and an authorised walkthrough; avoid taking powers for granted.
targeted: Walk through a senior family member's unexpected incapacity with the relevant officeholder. Confirm your duties and actual powers before discussing actions.
Verify emergency contacts, document locations and permitted access. Rehearse the first 48 hours, including a contact who is unavailable.

subdimensions.label: Stewardship & agency
subdimensions.action: Write what you would preserve, change and create. Test one proposed change against family purpose, affected people and the authority you would need.
subdimensions.progress: A reasoned stewardship proposal acknowledges consequences and leaves room for your own approach.
subdimensions.stretch: Sponsor a bounded improvement and test whether its results support your original intention.
subdimensions.blocked: Develop a proposal or learning project while awaiting authority to act.
targeted: Write what you would preserve, change and create. Test one proposed change against purpose, affected people and the authority needed.
Describe how you would fulfil a responsibility in your own way while respecting agreed duties. Discuss a practical example with an independent mentor.
